newsitem.title: USA: Stocks renew rally; Dow nears 8,000-point mark.
newsitem.headline: Stocks renew rally; Dow nears 8,000-point mark.

text.p: Stocks rose Monday, with momentum from last week's powerful rally carrying the Dow Jones industrial average closer to the 8,000-point mark.
At 1 p.m. EDT/1700 GMT, the Dow was up 18.09 points at 7,913.90, adding to last Thursday's record close of 7,895.81.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 14-12 on active volume of 290 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite rose 7.02 points to 1,474.63, boosted by strength in large technology stocks.
After pushing the Dow up 223 points during last week's shortened trading period, investors came back from Friday's Independence Day holiday break and picked up where they left off.
"Everybody likes to jump on a winning bandwagon," said Peter Coolidge, senior equity trader at Brean Murray & Co.

Gold stocks, however, were a sore spot for the market, taking a beating in line with a sharp decline in the price of the precious metal to a 12-year low of $317.50 an ounce on New York's Commodity Exchange.
Topping the NYSE's most active list were gold mining giants, Barrick Gold Corp., which fell 1-13/16 to 20-1/8, and Placer Dome Inc., down 2-1/16 to 14-1/8. Homestake Mining Co. was off 1/2 to 12-1/2.
Gold prices, which have lost $50 per ounce since the start of the year, received a new blow when Australia's central bank disclosed it had sold off 60 percent of its gold reserves.
The gold market is traditionally a safe haven for investors at times of high inflation and bear stock markets.

The turmoil in gold comes after June employment data issued Thursday confirmed Wall Street's expectations that the nation's economy was growing at a moderate pace without major inflationary pressures.
The employment data sparked a 100-point Dow rally Thursday. "It's a real positive time" for the stock market, said BT
Brokerage trader Paul Rich. "Things are really cooking."
Wall Street on Monday found itself in a lull between economic reports and the start of the second-quarter reporting season.
Friday's report on producer price inflation will be the next key dose of economic data.
On the earnings front, Motorola Inc. and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. are among the large companies that are due to report their results Tuesday.

Stocks were again supported by lower long-term interest rates. The 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was up nearly a full point, lowering its yield to 6.56 percent from 6.61 percent Thursday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.

"The bottom line is that we have a decent follow-through from Thursday's close," Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "The bonds seem to doing well and the sellers don't seem to want to be aggressive."
Among technology stocks, Intel Corp. rose 2-2/16 to 147-1/6, Microsoft Corp. gained 1-5/16 to 130-7/8, and Cisco Systems Inc. rose 2-4/16 to 73-13/16.
Pharmaceutical company Jones Medical Industries Inc. sank 15 to 28-3/8 after saying it expects its second-quarter earnings to fall below analysts' expectations.
Integrated Health Services Inc. fell 2-13/16 to 36-1/8 after saying it agreed to merge with with RoTech Medical Corp. in a deal valued at $915 million. RoTech rose 1-1/4 to 20-1/8.
